newsitem.title: GERMANY: Berlin court cites jobs, not names in Iran case.
newsitem.headline: Berlin court cites jobs, not names in Iran case.

text.p: A German court that on Thursday accused Iran's leadership of ordering a political killing in Berlin avoided citing names but gave the positions of the Tehran officials it believed were behind the attack.

The court said Tehran's Committee for Special Operations had ordered the crime and described its members as the state president, Iran's religious leader, the Ministry of Intelligence and other security officials.

The statement stopped just short of naming supreme religious leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, who prosecutors said had ordered the killings, and President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani, who they said approved the plan.
"The decision was taken by the Committee for Special Operations," presideing judge Frithjof Kubsch said as he read out the long opinion following the verdict.

The court gave the two main suspects life sentences and two accomplices jail terms of between five and 11 years for the gangland-style slaying of a group of dissident Iranian Kurdish leaders in Berlin's Mykonos restaurant.
Germany has already issued an arest warrant for Iranian Intelligence Minister Ali Fallahiyan, whose ministry was named as one of the members of the committee.
